newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU unveils new union-wide immigration policy plan.
newsitem.headline: EU unveils new union-wide immigration policy plan.

text.p: The European Union unveiled a new immigration plan on Wednesday to allow non-EU citizens who have lived in the 15-country bloc for over five years to apply for residency and invite their families to join them.
The new plan, part of a wider bid to draw up a single EU policy for non-citizens seeking residence and work rights, needs the support of all 15 member states to become binding.
"The world is today seeing great migration movements and this migration is part of international cooperation," EU justice commissioner Anita Gradin told a news conference.
"We need clear rules for people seeking jobs, reunifying their families, students," she said, stressing the plan would not in itself lead to an increase in the number of immigrants.
Under the proposal, family members of a non-EU citizen turned resident would be allowed to work within the EU after living in the country for six months.

Gradin said nearly 13 million non-EU citizens lived in the Union and over one million people entered the Union every year, either as immigrants or to seek temporary protection during a crisis in their own country.
The plan does not cover asylum-seekers.
A foreigner would only be allowed to work in the EU if the post could not be filled by an EU citizen or one who had earned his residency after the five-year stint, the plan said.
These contract workers would be entitled to a one-year renewable residence permit.
If the plan is agreed, self-employed foreigners will have to prove they have means and will have a positive impact on the EU's job market.
Seasonal workers, looking for work such as grape picking or ski resort attendants, would be given a six month visa.
Pensioners, artists and writers would be eligible for a one-year permit if they showed they had enough money or social security cover to support themselves. 301547 GMT jul 97
